validity.recommendation: no action on existence/classification — well documented
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE and CLASSIFICATION strongly confirmed, independent of GEM/wiki material. Original FERC certificate proceeding documented directly: Federal Register notice E7-8519 (2007-05-04, DEIS notice of availability, Docket Nos. CP07-44-000/CP07-45-000, PF06-28-000) and E8-298 (2008-01-10, NRCS Record of Decision notice, 73 FR 1862) — the latter states 'On December 18, 2006, SESH filed, in Docket No. CP07-446-000, an application with the Commission pursuant to section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act ... for a Certificate to construct, operate, and maintain an interstate natural gas pipeline', and independently corroborates the route as 'approximately 269 miles'. A 2007-era PHMSA MAOP waiver petition (downloads.regulations.gov/PHMSA-2007-27607-0002/attachment_1.pdf, SESH's own regulatory filing) gives full engineering detail (mileposts, compressor stations, diameters, MAOPs). Rigzone (prefiling-era, ~2006) and a Houston Chronicle/PRNewswire release (2006-12-08) independently describe the same project (developers Duke Energy Gas Transmission/CenterPoint Energy Gas Transmission, joined later by Southern Natural Gas for the first 115 miles), consistent chronology. Post-construction, three separate Natural Gas Intelligence articles (2007-05-21, 2008-09-08, 2008-09-10) track FERC's phased in-service authorizations. Current operator disclosures (Enbridge factsheet PDF p.85; Energy Transfer FY2023 10-K, which lists SESH among its 'principal interstate transportation ... assets', 'a 50/50 joint venture with Enbridge Inc., provides transportation services in Louisiana, Mississippi and Alabama') confirm it is still an active, FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transmission pipeline as of FY2023. Not a phantom, not GEM-only, correctly classified as Fuel=Gas transmission. Opened 5 of the wiki page's 9 harvested citations in some form (Enbridge factsheet, EIA nav-page landing check, Chron PR, infopost.enbridge.com tariff portal live-check, businesswire.com 2014 release — the last 403's/inaccessible via scripted client); did not deep-read the 2015 Barclays presentation PDF, a 2017 Enable Midstream investor-presentation PDF, an Enbridge-Spectra merger release, or a Duke Energy history page — not needed given the stronger, more specific primary sources found independently (FERC/Federal Register dockets, PHMSA petition, SEC 10-K, Rigzone, Chron/PRNewswire, NGI).

DUPLICATE check against the 50-pipeline roster: no other roster row plausibly describes this same physical line (Perryville Hub, LA → Gulfstream system, Mobile County, AL). Informational note only, not a roster match: search results surfaced a confusingly similarly-named but entirely DIFFERENT and unrelated NEW pipeline project, 'Southeast Supply Enhancement' (Transco/Williams, FERC Docket PF24-2-000, ~55 miles, ~$1.53B, approved ~early 2026) — confirmed this is NOT P0164 and has no PID on the roster; flagged only to prevent a future name-collision, not staged as a discovery/cross-row lead since it isn't in-scope for this batch. A GEM-surface search hit (api.globalenergymonitor.org/assets/P0164) also surfaced and was disregarded per the standing rule against ever citing/relying on GEM's own surfaces.

validity.researcher_notes: Sheet stages Owner2 = 'Enable Midstream Partners LP' (50%). This is stale: Energy Transfer LP completed its acquisition of Enable Midstream Partners in December 2021, and Enable Midstream Partners LP has not existed as a separate ownership entity since. Two independent CURRENT primary sources, each an owner speaking about its own asset (satisfies the co-owner-independence rule), agree: (1) Enbridge's own current asset factsheet PDF (p.85 of 156): 'Ownership: Enbridge (50%); Energy Transfer LP (50%)... Operator: Enbridge (business and technical functions), Energy Transfer LP (field operations)'; (2) Energy Transfer's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024, SEC EDGAR): defines 'SESH' as 'Southeast Supply Header Pipeline and/or Southeast Supply Header, LLC, a non-wholly owned subsidiary of Energy Transfer' and separately states 'SESH, a 50/50 joint venture with Enbridge Inc., provides transportation services in Louisiana, Mississippi and Alabama.' No source found still attributes an ownership stake to Enable Midstream Partners LP as a going concern. This is a genuine, high-confidence attribution defect, not a caveat — recommend Baird apply the correction rather than the agent editing the value column directly.

validity.recommendation: no action on the current LengthKnown=462.00 km — well supported; historical divergence documented for context only
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current LengthKnown = 462.00 km (287 mi), which is well corroborated by two independent current operator disclosures: Enbridge's factsheet ('Length: 287 miles (462 km)') and Energy Transfer's FY2023 10-K (pipeline-systems table: 'Southeast Supply Header ("SESH") 50% 290 1.1 —', i.e. ~290 route-miles, a rounder figure consistent with 287/462 km). HOWEVER, every source describing the ORIGINAL 2006-2008 certificated build states a materially different figure of ~269-270 miles: the PHMSA MAOP waiver petition ('the SESH Project will consist of 269 miles of 36-inch and 42-inch diameter [pipe]', itemized as 104.1 mi of 42-in + 164.4 mi of 36-in), the NRCS Federal Register Record of Decision notice ('extends for approximately 269 miles'), Rigzone's 2006 prefiling-era article ('270-mile, 36-inch diameter gas pipeline'), and two 2008 NGI articles ('213 miles of its 270-mile pipeline', 'about 270 miles of 36- to 42-inch diameter pipeline'). The ~17-21 mile / 6-7% gap between the original-certificate figure and the current 287-290 mi figure is plausibly explained by a subsequent capacity/diameter expansion — a Dec 2006 PRNewswire release (chron.com) describes Southern Natural Gas buying into the first 115 miles and upgrading its diameter from 36-in to 42-in to add 140 MMcf/d of capacity, and further FERC amendment dockets likely added laterals/looping between 2008 and today — but this was not independently traced docket-by-docket within budget. Recommend treating the current 462 km/287 mi as correct (high tier, current) and NOT reverting to the 269-270 mi original-certificate figure; flagging the historical gap only so a future researcher isn't surprised by the older sources' smaller number.

cross_row_leads.facts: Roster lists P0199 Gulfstream Natural Gas Pipeline with Capacity=1310.00 MMcf/d and LengthKnown=1199.00 km. The current (2024-dated content) Enbridge factsheet's Gulfstream section states: 'Length: 745 miles (1,199 km)' (exact match) and 'Peak day capacity: 1.31 Bcf/d' = 1,310 MMcf/d (exact match to the CURRENT GEM value). This directly conflicts with whatever finding led P0199's own already-staged shard (batches/united-states-gas/staging/deepsweep-gulf-operating/rows/P0199.json) to flag Capacity=1310 as 'stale' and recommend 1378 MMcf/d 'post-2022 Phase VI expansion' — this current Enbridge factsheet still says 1.31 Bcf/d, not 1.378. Whoever reconciles P0199 should weigh this operator-current factsheet against whatever FERC/trade-press source produced the 1378 figure; not resolved here, flagged only.

Roster lists P0223 Nautilus Gas Pipeline with LengthKnown=154.00 km, EndLocation 'Neptune Gas Processing Plant, St. Mary's Parish, Louisiana'. The Enbridge factsheet states the Nautilus Pipeline is '115 miles (185 km) ... 96 miles (154 km) offshore, 19 miles (31 km) onshore' delivering 'to a processing plant near Garden City, LA'. GEM's 154.00 km exactly matches only the OFFSHORE portion of the system, not the 185 km total — i.e. GEM's Length appears to omit the 19-mile/31 km onshore lateral to the processing plant, even though GEM's own EndLocation names that same onshore plant as the row's terminus. Worth a targeted check: either GEM's Length should be 185 km total (if the row is meant to span offshore+onshore to the plant it names as its endpoint), or the plant-name endpoint should be corrected to the offshore delivery platform if the row is deliberately offshore-only. Also note a possible facility-name mismatch: Enbridge says the plant is 'near Garden City, LA' while GEM names it 'Neptune Gas Processing Plant, St. Mary's Parish' — may be the same facility under different names, not verified here.

Roster lists P0217 Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline with LengthKnown=44.50 MILES (LengthKnownUnits='mi') and Capacity=800.00 MMcf/d. The current Enbridge factsheet states: 'Length: 44.5 miles (71.6 km)' and 'Capacity: 800 MMcf/d' — an EXACT match on both figures once units are read correctly. This appears to CORRECT, not confirm, a concern already staged in P0192's own shard (batches/united-states-gas/staging/deepsweep-gulf-operating/rows/P0192.json), which flagged P0217's 44.5 value as if it were mislabeled km (reasoning from a 2008 archived source's '45 mi' figure and assuming GEM's LengthKnownUnits was 'km'). Checking the live worklist shows LengthKnownUnits is actually 'mi' for P0217, so no unit-mislabeling error exists here — recommend closing that specific worry when P0217 is swept, while still independently checking whether the broader 'units mix-up across the Enbridge-offshore family' hypothesis holds for any OTHER roster rows (it does not appear to for this one).

Roster lists P0249 Sabal Trail Gas Transmission Pipeline with LengthKnown=516.00 MILES and Capacity=830.00 MMcf/d. The current Enbridge factsheet states: 'Length: 517 miles of 36-inch- and 24-inch-diameter pipeline' (near-exact match to 516 mi — confirms the value, no action needed) but 'Peak day capacity: 1.03 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d)' = 1,030 MMcf/d, materially higher than GEM's 830.00 MMcf/d. Sabal Trail's capacity is publicly known to have grown via compression-only expansions after its 2017 in-service date (no new pipe, i.e. would not change LengthKnown), so 830 MMcf/d may reflect the original build while 1,030 MMcf/d reflects a later expansion phase. Also notes Ownership 'Sabal Trail Transmission, LLC (100%), a joint venture of Enbridge, NextEra Energy, Inc., and Duke Energy Corporation' and 'Operator: Enbridge' for cross-checking P0249's Owner/Operator cells. Not resolved here, flagged for P0249's own capacity-expansion research.

Roster lists P0175 Destin Gas Pipeline with LengthKnown=385.00 MILES. The current Enbridge factsheet states the Destin Pipeline 'travels a distance of 255 miles (410 km)—with an offshore segment of 120 miles (193 km) in the Gulf of Mexico, and an onshore segment of 135 miles (217 km) in Mississippi', Capacity 1.2 Bcf/d (matches GEM's 1200.00 MMcf/d exactly), diameter 24-to-36-in (matches GEM's '24, 36'). GEM's LengthKnown=385 mi does not match the factsheet's 255 mi total, nor either sub-segment alone (120 or 135 mi), nor their sum — a ~130-mile / 51% gap with no obvious unit-conversion or segment-scope explanation from this source alone. Also note the factsheet says Enbridge holds only a 33% interest in Destin (operated by joint-venture partner Third Coast Midstream), useful for cross-checking P0175's Owner/Operator cells. Worth a dedicated length re-check when P0175 is swept; not resolved here.

summary: P0164 Southeast Supply Header: existence/classification/non-duplicate all confirmed high-tier against FERC/Federal-Register/PHMSA/SEC/trade-press sources fully independent of GEM. Two concerns staged: attribution (Owner2 'Enable Midstream Partners LP' is stale, corrected by 2 independent current co-owner sources to 'Energy Transfer LP') and a spec caveat (current Length 462 km/287 mi is well-supported, but every original-certificate-era source states ~269-270 mi — documented as historical context, no value change recommended). All 14 worklist units given proposed refs: 11 REFS_ADDED (Status, Fuel, Proposal 2006-12, Construction 2007-11, Start month=9, Capacity 1140 MMcf/d, Pressure 1200/1250/1300 psig, Length, Diameter, Location, SegmentCost $842M, Operator) plus 1 UNRESOLVED (Owner — not sourcing the stale current value; see attribution concern). Nothing left UNRESOLVED for lack of research — SegmentCost, which looked headed for UNRESOLVED, was resolved via SESH's own PHMSA MAOP-waiver petition ('$842 million'), a genuine primary source independent of the GEM-wiki-cited EIA navigation page. Staged 5 cross_row_leads from exhaustive reading of the Enbridge asset factsheet: P0199 Gulfstream (current factsheet capacity 1.31 Bcf/d conflicts with P0199's own staged 1378 MMcf/d finding), P0223 Nautilus (GEM's 154 km may capture only the offshore portion of a 185 km offshore+onshore system), P0217 Mississippi Canyon (corrects a unit-mislabeling worry raised in P0192's shard — P0217's 44.5 mi is actually exact and correct), P0249 Sabal Trail (length confirmed near-exact; capacity 830 MMcf/d looks stale against the factsheet's 1.03 Bcf/d), and P0175 Destin (385 mi vs. the factsheet's 255 mi total — unexplained ~130 mi gap).
